courses: Conducting research on AI safety, adversarial robustness and model evaluation for machine learning systems under the supervision of Prof. Alessio Lomuscio, including conversational LLM agents, RAG systems, and decision-tree ensembles.
Supported by the UKRI Centre for Doctoral Training in Safe and Trusted Artificial Intelligence.

work.name: Safe Intelligence Ltd.
highlights: Core contributor at an Imperial College London spinout for the product design and R&D of a SaaS product for testing and validation of AI agents.

Designed iterative, optimisation-based methods for multi-turn jailbreaking of AI agents, achieving an attack success rate of up to 50% against Sonnet 5, GPT-5.6, and Gemini 3.6-powered agents evaluated on HarmBench behaviours, exposing alignment failures that emerge over extended interactions.

Developed optimisation-based black-box methods that generate intent-preserving adversarial queries to stress-test RAG agents, eliciting evidence-contradicting intrinsic hallucinations in up to 54% of responses from GPT-5 and Gemini 3 models.
Led the synthetic test-data generation workstream, designing methods to achieve broad domain coverage for systematic agent evaluation.
Proposed and implemented a robust gradient boosting algorithm for tabular data models, improving robust accuracy by 44% over the state of the art and 113% over conventional XGBoost.

work.name: Pangaea Data Ltd.
highlights: Directed a four-person cross-functional NLP and product team to identify patients with rare diseases from electronic health records, collaborating with clinicians and stakeholders to refine research objectives and validate product design.

Designed a clinical NLP pipeline that used BERT-based models and regex keyword detection to mine unstructured text, extract ontology concepts, and identify patients through a decision-tree model, distributed on Microsoft Azure Marketplace.

Led a proof of concept for a major pharmaceutical company, applying the pipeline to data from approximately 65,000 patients to identify cohorts with cachexia, COPD, and lupus nephritis; the approach identified 2-5x as many patients compared to a diagnostic code baseline.
Authored technical white papers, research grant submissions and project proposals leading to 2 POCs.
